title: Business Economics
modules: Unit I: Introduction to Business Economics: nature and scope; objectives and theory of the firm; economic way of thinking; optimization techniques and economic decision making

Unit II: Demand Analysis: utility; demand and supply; market equilibrium; consumer and producer surplus; price controls; elasticity of demand; indifference curves, budget constraint, consumer's equilibrium; price, income and substitution effects
Unit III: Demand forecasting: purpose, quantitative and qualitative techniques, criteria for a good method

Unit IV: Production Analysis: cost concepts; production functions (linear, Leontief, Cobb-Douglas); law of variable proportions and returns to scale; isoquant and isocost; producer's equilibrium; industry analysis; cost-oriented pricing
Unit V: Market Analysis: perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly; output and pricing; entry and exit; game theory; global economic climate

sessions.topic: Introduction to managerial economics, principles and optimization
Market forces: demand and supply, consumer and producer surplus, equilibrium
Elasticity of demand; indifference curves, budget constraint, consumer's equilibrium; price, income and substitution effects

note: The syllabus has units, not a session-by-session plan, and no weightage table. The 2025 MST asked about the production possibility curve, ordinal utility, the budget line, elasticity and exponential smoothing, which have no deck in the folders yet.
